name: Sharm El Sheikh
tagline: Egypt's largest Red Sea resort town, built around extraordinary coral reefs and some of the best diving conditions on Earth.
highlight: Drifting over Ras Mohammed's coral wall, a sheer drop into deep blue water lined with more fish species than seems possible in one place.
shortDescription: Egypt's largest Red Sea resort town, home to Ras Mohammed National Park and some of the most extraordinary coral reef diving and snorkelling on Earth.
metaDescription: A Sharm El Sheikh travel guide: Ras Mohammed National Park, Naama Bay, diving and snorkelling, food and how to plan a Red Sea resort trip.
knownFor: World-class diving, coral reefs, Naama Bay

image.alt: The South Sinai coastline near Sharm El Sheikh

intro: Sharm El Sheikh is Egypt's largest and best-developed Red Sea resort town, built along the southern tip of the Sinai Peninsula where the desert meets some of the most extraordinary coral reefs on Earth.
Its real draw is underwater — extraordinary visibility, healthy coral and a density of marine species that has made this coastline one of the world's premier diving destinations for decades.
Most visitors base themselves around Naama Bay or a nearby resort strip, splitting time between diving or snorkelling trips to Ras Mohammed National Park and simply relaxing by the Red Sea itself.

whyVisit.intro: Sharm El Sheikh's case rests on being one of the world's great diving and snorkelling destinations, with resort infrastructure to match.

points.title: Ras Mohammed is one of the world's best dive sites
points.text: Extraordinary coral walls and visibility at the meeting point of two seas.

points.title: The coral reefs here are remarkably healthy
points.text: Some of the best-preserved reef systems left in the Red Sea.

points.title: It's accessible to every experience level
points.text: From beginner snorkellers to advanced technical divers, all well catered for.

points.title: The resort infrastructure is well developed
points.text: A wide range of hotels, restaurants and dive centres to suit any budget.

points.title: It works well as a Red Sea extension to a Nile-focused trip
points.text: A direct flight connects easily to Cairo or elsewhere in Egypt.

attractionsIntro: Sharm El Sheikh's essential sights are mostly underwater, at some of the Red Sea's finest reef locations.

attractions.name: Naama Bay

image.alt: Naama Bay in Sharm El Sheikh

attractions.text: The town's main hub, a curving bay lined with hotels, restaurants and dive centres right on the water.
attractions.tip: A lively spot for an evening stroll, with restaurants spanning every cuisine and budget.

attractions.name: Ras Mohammed National Park

image.alt: Ras Mohammed National Park near Sharm El Sheikh

attractions.text: One of the world's premier dive and snorkel sites, where the Gulf of Aqaba and Gulf of Suez meet in extraordinary biodiversity.
attractions.tip: Book a full-day boat trip here rather than a rushed half-day for the best experience.

attractions.name: The reef's coral formations

image.alt: Coral reef formations near Sharm El Sheikh

attractions.text: Remarkably healthy and colourful, among the best-preserved coral systems remaining in the Red Sea.
attractions.tip: Never touch or stand on coral — it's a fragile, slow-growing ecosystem.

attractions.name: Clownfish in sea anemones

image.file: File:Pez payaso (Amphiprion bicinctus) en una anémona magnífica (Heteractis magnifica), mar Rojo, Egipto, 2023-04-18, DD 93.jpg
image.alt: Clownfish sheltering in a sea anemone in the Red Sea

attractions.text: A reliable, delightful sighting for snorkellers and divers alike across the reef.
attractions.tip: Watch quietly from a respectful distance — clownfish are territorial and can nip if disturbed.

attractions.name: Hawksbill sea turtles

image.file: File:Tortuga carey (Eretmochelys imbricata), parque nacional Ras Muhammad, Egipto, 2022-03-28, DD 56.jpg
image.alt: A hawksbill sea turtle in the Red Sea

attractions.text: A real, if not guaranteed, highlight of many dives and snorkel trips around Ras Mohammed.
attractions.tip: Never chase or touch a turtle — observe patiently and let it approach on its own terms.

attractions.name: Naama Bay's beach
attractions.text: A relaxed stretch of sand right in the centre of town, easy access for a swim between other activities.
attractions.tip: Most resort beaches are private to guests, though public access points exist nearby.

attractions.name: The reef's moray eels

image.file: File:Morey Eel in Red Sea, Naama Bay, Sharm-el-Sheikh.jpg
image.alt: A moray eel in the Red Sea near Sharm El Sheikh

attractions.text: A common sighting for divers exploring the reef's crevices and coral overhangs.
attractions.tip: A good subject for underwater photography, if you keep a safe, respectful distance.

thingsToDoIntro: Sharm El Sheikh exists for its underwater world, though plenty of relaxation rounds out a visit.

thingsToDo.title: Dive or snorkel Ras Mohammed

image.file: File:Coral (Favia favus), parque nacional Ras Muhammad, Egipto, 2022-03-27, DD 12.jpg
image.alt: Coral at Ras Mohammed National Park

thingsToDo.text: An essential Sharm El Sheikh experience, exploring some of the Red Sea's finest reef at this protected national park.
thingsToDo.tip: Book with a PADI or SSI certified dive centre, especially for anything beyond snorkelling.

thingsToDo.title: Spot clownfish in anemones

image.file: File:Peces payaso (Amphiprion bicinctus) en una anémona magnífica (Heteractis magnifica), parque nacional Ras Muhammad, Egipto, 2022-03-27, DD 35.jpg
image.alt: Clownfish in an anemone at Ras Mohammed

thingsToDo.text: A delightful, accessible sighting even for first-time snorkellers.
thingsToDo.tip: Bring an underwater camera or housing — this is one of the reef's most photogenic residents.

thingsToDo.title: Watch for sea turtles while snorkelling

image.file: File:Tortuga carey (Eretmochelys imbricata), parque nacional Ras Muhammad, Egipto, 2022-03-28, DD 56.jpg
image.alt: Snorkelling near a sea turtle in the Red Sea

thingsToDo.text: A memorable moment for many visitors, spotting a hawksbill turtle gliding gracefully over the reef.
thingsToDo.tip: Stay calm and still — sudden movements tend to send turtles swimming away quickly.

thingsToDo.title: Relax on Naama Bay's beach

image.file: File:Sharm el Sheikh Naama Bay - panoramio (10).jpg
image.alt: Relaxing on the beach at Naama Bay

thingsToDo.text: An easy way to balance out days of diving, simple beach time right in the centre of town.
thingsToDo.tip: Most resorts offer sun loungers and water sports right on the sand.

thingsToDo.title: Look for moray eels on a dive

image.file: File:Morey Eel in Red Sea, Naama Bay, Sharm-el-Sheikh.jpg

thingsToDo.text: An exciting find for divers exploring the reef's nooks and coral formations.
thingsToDo.tip: Ask your dive guide to point out likely moray hiding spots along the route.

thingsToDo.title: Explore the reef's angelfish

image.file: File:Pez ángel real (Pygoplites diacanthus), parque nacional Ras Muhammad, Egipto, 2022-03-26, DD 155.jpg
image.alt: A royal angelfish on the reef near Sharm El Sheikh

thingsToDo.text: A colourful highlight of any dive or snorkel trip, angelfish among the reef's most striking residents.
thingsToDo.tip: Their vivid colours make them a rewarding subject for underwater photography.

foods.whereToTry: Restaurants throughout Naama Bay and the wider resort strip.

foods.name: Koshari

image.alt: Koshari, Egypt's national dish of rice, lentils and pasta

foods.name: Ful medames

foods.whereToTry: Cafés and resort breakfasts throughout Sharm El Sheikh.

foods.whereToTry: Restaurants and street stalls throughout Sharm El Sheikh.

foods.name: Karkade (hibiscus tea)

foods.whereToTry: Cafés and restaurants throughout the resort area.

bestTime.headline: March to May and September to November for the most comfortable diving conditions
bestTime.summary: Sharm El Sheikh is a year-round destination, with water temperatures staying warm even in winter.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Sharm El Sheikh visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Book with a PADI or SSI certified dive centre for any diving beyond snorkelling.
Bring your own certification card if you're a qualified diver.
Pack reef-safe sunscreen to help protect the coral.
Never touch or stand on coral — it's a fragile, slow-growing ecosystem.
Stay hydrated and use sun protection, even on overcast days on the water.
Book a Ras Mohammed trip a day or two ahead through your resort or a dive centre.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Sharm El Sheikh?
faq.a: Four to five days allows for multiple dive or snorkel trips alongside real relaxation time.

faq.q: Do you need to be a certified diver to visit?
faq.a: No, not — excellent snorkelling is available for non-divers, and beginner dive courses are widely offered.

faq.q: Is Ras Mohammed worth the trip?
faq.a: Yes — it's considered one of the world's premier dive and snorkel sites, with extraordinary visibility and marine life.

faq.q: What is Sharm El Sheikh known for?
faq.a: World-class Red Sea diving and snorkelling, alongside a well-developed resort scene at Naama Bay.

faq.q: Is Sharm El Sheikh good for beginners?
faq.a: Yes — the resort has extensive infrastructure for every experience level, from first-time snorkellers to advanced divers.

faq.q: Can you combine Sharm El Sheikh with the Nile Valley?
faq.a: Yes, easily — a direct flight connects to Cairo, making it a natural Red Sea extension to a Nile-focused Egypt trip.
